name: Work toward your first pull-up
blurb: A trainable, unambiguous goal. The route is not endless attempts but a structured progression: hangs, scapular pulls, negatives and assisted reps.
gear: A resistance band or a low bar for rows
steps: Build a dead hang to 30 seconds. Grip is often the first limit.
Learn scapular pulls: hanging, pull your shoulder blades down and back without bending your arms. This is the missing piece for most people.
Do slow negatives: jump or step to the top position and lower over five seconds. Three sets of three, twice a week.
Add band-assisted or ring-row work as volume, progressing to steeper rows.
Test once a fortnight — not every session, because testing is not training.
Once you get one, build to three sets of three before chasing bigger numbers.
tips: Two or three sessions a week with recovery between beats daily attempts, which just accumulate fatigue.
Body weight matters. A few kilograms lost shows up here more than in any other lift.
Kipping is a different skill. Learn the strict version first.
proof: One strict pull-up from a dead hang, chin clearly over the bar, no swinging.
